name: Jacalteco
confidence_why: Day 1973 places stress on the first syllable of the stem and Bennett 2016 and DiCanio & Bennett describe Popti' stress as word-initial but shifting to the final syllable phrase-finally, whereas the 2007 OKMA/ALMG normative grammar (Delgado Rojas et al.) states final stress on words in isolation, which is that same phrase-final position, so initial word stress is the better-supported reading although a modern first-hand grammar contradicts it.
catalog_quote: Stress occurs obligatorily on the first syllable of most stems, on the syllable before a contour except in emphatic sentences and yes-no questions, and on a lexically determined syllable of some polysyllabic loans. (Day 1973:20)

new_statements.quote: 3 Acento. El Popti' es uno de los idiomas con acento fijo, las palabras independientes se acentúan en la última sílaba; es decir, posee un acento agudo. Sin embargo en el idioma el acento no se representa dentro de la escritura porque no existen palabras cuyo significado dependan de la acentuación. En los ejemplos se resalta con negrilla la sílaba acentuada. a[wal] milpa / in[tam] iguana / aht[zoq'] jolote / el[q'om] ladrón / chintxu[mu] lo entiendo. Los préstamos, también toman el acento del Popti' como parte de su incorporación al mismo y tampoco se acentúan gráficamente. xhi[lah] silla / ken[yah] guineo, banano / pe[ch'an] guacal, cabeza calva / ja[han] hincado / chin saj[chi] juego. (p. 51; brackets mark the syllables printed in bold)
new_statements.translation: 3 Stress. Popti' is one of the languages with fixed stress; independent words are stressed on the last syllable, that is, it has oxytone (final) stress. However, in the language stress is not represented in the writing because there are no words whose meaning depends on stress placement. In the examples the stressed syllable is highlighted in bold. a[WAL] 'maize field' / in[TAM] 'iguana' / aht[ZOQ'] 'turkey' / el[Q'OM] 'thief' / chintxu[MU] 'I understand it'. Loanwords also take Popti' stress as part of their incorporation into the language and likewise are not marked for stress in writing: xhi[LAH] 'chair' / ken[YAH] 'banana' / pe[CH'AN] 'gourd, bald head' / ja[HAN] 'kneeling' / chin saj[CHI] 'game'.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog records Jacalteco from StressTyp2 (StressTyp2) with initial stress, i.e. fixed INITIAL stress (per StressTyp2's reading of Day 1973:20, 'first syllable of most stems'). The ALMG/OKMA normative grammar states fixed FINAL stress on independent words, with ten bolded examples all final and loans re-stressed to final. Same language (Popti'/Jacalteco), different fixed edge: initial vs final.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Fixed stress on the last syllable of every independent word (oxytone), including inflected verb forms (chintxuMU) and Spanish loans, which are re-stressed to final position (xhiLAH < silla, kenYAH < guinea). Stress is never contrastive, so the orthography does not mark it. The bold syllable in every one of the ten examples is the final one (verified from the PDF font runs).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the only qualification is 'palabras independientes' (independent words), implying that clitics/dependent words are outside the rule. Loans are explicitly said to conform. The introduction (p. 27-28) repeats that stress is not written 'puesto que no se han encontrado palabras cuyo significado dependa del acento' (since no words have been found whose meaning depends on stress).
new_statements.identity_note: The grammar is the normative (standard) grammar of Popti' prepared by the Comunidad Lingüística Popti' of ALMG with OKMA, built on a 2002-2003 dialect survey of all Popti' variants (pp. 20-25); the stress rule is stated for the language as a whole, with no dialect restriction. 'Jakalteka-Popti'' = Jacalteco = Glottolog popt1235.

readall_conflicts: The one work opened, the 2007 OKMA/ALMG Gramática Normativa Popti' (p. 51), states fixed final (oxytone) stress on independent words and shows it on ten examples including loans; the catalog's only record (StressTyp2, initial stress) codes fixed initial stress, tracing to StressTyp2's reading of Day 1973 ('first syllable of most stems'). These are direct opposites at the word level. Neither Day 1973 nor Craig 1977 could be opened in this or the previous check (lending-only / paywalled), so the initial-stress claim has not been checked against its source text; the Aissen 2000 postprint held by the project mentions only 'the last stressed syllable before the juncture' and does not locate word stress. A possible reconciliation, not stated by any opened source, is that StressTyp2's 'stem-initial' and the grammar's 'word-final' describe different domains (bare CVC stems are simultaneously initial and final; the grammar's chintxuMU and loan examples decide for word-final in longer words).

audit.recode_to: contested initial~final: either keep initial (initial stress) downgraded from fixed-strict with contra + phrase-final caution (Tojolabal tojo1241 precedent in this catalog codes the phrase-medial/word-level initial pattern), or reclassify as final (final stress) per OKMA 2007:51 'palabras independientes se acentúan en la última sílaba'; owner's call after reading Day 1973 pp.20-24
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the two quotations the record actually carries (DiCanio & Bennett preprint p.10; Day 1973:20 as relayed by the StressTyp2 entry for this language) are both present verbatim in copies we hold at the stated locators, and Bennett 2016 p.495 is confirmed too. The classification (initial, weight-blind, word domain with a phrase-final/pre-contour prominence noted separately and loanword exceptions) matches every source opened: StressTyp2 Initial, WALS 14A Initial/15A Fixed, and both Mayanist surveys ('normally on the first syllable of the word or root'). Nothing found suggests the classification is wrong, and the specialist literature as of 2016-2018 still cites only Day 1973 for Popti' stress, so no better stress description is known to exist — hence 'adequate' rather than 'at-risk'. It is not 'well-sourced' because the primary (Day 1973 p.20) has never been opened by us; the grade is quotation carried over second-hand from StressTyp2 via a database. Tw

sources.quote: "Phrasally-determined stress: Several languages in the Q'anjob'alan subgroup of Western Mayan have variable stress conditioned by phrasal position: stress is normally on the first syllable of the word or root, but shifts to the final syllable in phrase-final position. Phrasally-conditioned stress is well-documented for Q'anjob'al (5), and its close relatives Akatek and Popti' (Day 1973, England 2001)." (DiCanio & Bennett, Prosody in Mesoamerican Languages, preprint p. 10,)
